Subject: Thanks for the discovery — proposed eval kickoff times

Hi Emily / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. To recap quickly: Acme is evaluating a private/secure trial to validate prompt latency, multi-user routing, and cost per 1k tokens across your customer-facing summarization flows. Success criteria you mentioned were: <1s median token latency for 512-token prompts, end-to-end cost < $0.003/token, and no PII leakage in generated summaries.

Next step from our side is to kick off a short evaluation (2-week pilot) with a technical deep dive to align trial plan and access. Proposed times for an evaluation kickoff + tech deep dive (30-45m):
- Wed, Mar 4, 9:00-9:45am PT
- Thu, Mar 5, 10:00-10:45am PT
- Fri, Mar 6, 2:00-2:45pm PT

Can you confirm which slot works and whether your infra lead (Tom) can join? I’ll have Marissa (solutions engineer) join to walk trial plan and daisy-chain the prompt set/eval approach.

I attached a short trial plan draft for your review (acme-trial-plan-v1.pdf). If those objectives look correct, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short checklist for access (API keys, sample prompt corpus, test account).

Thanks — Neha

Hi Emily / Neha,

Perfect — I’ll cover the trial plan and the evaluation approach in the kickoff. For sampling: a 5k-row sample is great for initial latency and quality baselines. For quality regression detection we usually ask for:
- 1-2 canonical prompts + 200-500 representative examples for focused evals
- 1k-5k broader sample for latency/throughput profiling

I’ll bring a short checklist and a proposed prompt-set split (dev/eval/prod) to the meeting. Also will note required access (test account, sandbox keys, IP allowlist if you want private deployment).

See you Wed at 9am PT — I’ll send the calendar invite in a few minutes.

Thanks,
Marissa
